was: St. Martin Parish facility at Butte La Rose in the Atchafalaya Basin. 17 paved full-hookup sites (one 50-amp, rest 30-amp) with water/sewer/fire rings, lined up along the water; boat launch on the bayou. Reservable online (Campspot); ~$30/night as of Aug 2025. --Claude
note: St. Martin Parish campground at Butte La Rose in the Atchafalaya Basin, with a boat launch on the bayou and paved sites with fire rings lined up along the water; one site has 50-amp power and the rest 30-amp. --Claude

note: Overnight RV park run by Streamside off I-20 at Monroe, beside a small lake on the property, with big-rig pull-throughs and a game room; the laundry is open 24 hours. --Claude

was: 36-site coastal RV resort off SH-35 between Rockport and Aransas Pass; all-concrete streets and pads, 30/50-amp full hookups plus cable, bathhouse and laundry. Daily/weekly/monthly stays, book via Campspot. Boat ramp on Aransas Bay nearby. --Claude

was: Marina RV park on Lake Palestine ~10 min south of Chandler. ~50 RV sites, most full hookups (30/50A), back-ins with fire rings; some sites on the water where you can pull a boat up to the pad. Store/bait, double boat launch, covered & open slips, fish-cleaning station; gated with coded access; tent sites and 2 cabins also. Reservable online (Campspot). --Claude
note: Marina RV park on Lake Palestine about 10 minutes south of Chandler, with back-in sites with fire rings, most of them with full hookups and some on the water where you can pull a boat up to the pad. was: Camper's World RV park inside the historic Fort Clark Springs community at Brackettville; open to transient RV travelers (not members-only). 85 full-hookup sites on level pea-gravel, RVs to ~50 ft, live-oak shade; laundry, community room. Guests get access to the spring-fed Las Moras Springs pool, 18-hole golf, and fort-grounds trails. Reservable online (Campspot/RoverPass). --Claude
note: Camper's World RV park inside the historic Fort Clark Springs community at Brackettville, open to travelers as well as members, with level pea-gravel sites under live oaks and a community room.  Guests can use the spring-fed Las Moras Springs pool, the 18-hole golf course and the trails on the fort grounds. --Claude
